rationale: The workflow runs on pull_request and push to rolling, so repeated commits to the same branch or PR can spawn superseded runs that consume runner time while an updated revision is already queued or in progress. Adding a concurrency group with cancel-in-progress cancels the older run for the same workflow branch/PR (using github.head_ref for pull requests and github.ref for push/schedule), preserving all matrix build/test coverage and required checks without weakening permissions or adding network access. This matches the P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE pattern (stale run cancellation), whose preconditions are satisfied: runs represent the same workflow and branch/PR, and a newer revision supersedes older checks. No release/deployment work is involved, and distinct branches are isolated by the concurrency group key.
